questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Lithospheric Plates and Earth Movements' refers to.
questions.a: Slabs of the Earth's crust move extremely slowly driven by thermal convection currents within mantle magma, dividing tectonic activity into endogenic and exogenic forces.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lithospheric Plates and Earth Movements'.
questions.a: Internal mantle convection propels crustal plate movement and drives endogenic and exogenic geological processes.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Lithospheric Plates and Earth Movements' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Earth Movements (source: gess203.txt lines 1-35)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Volcanoes and Volcanic Eruptions' refers to.
questions.a: A vent or opening in the earth's crust through which subterranean magma, molten rock, hot gases, and ash erupt suddenly.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Volcanoes and Volcanic Eruptions'.
questions.a: Deep subterranean pressure forces molten rock through crustal vents to form volcanic structures.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Volcanoes and Volcanic Eruptions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Volcanoes (source: gess203.txt lines 36-50)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Earthquakes and Seismic Energy Transmission' refers to.
questions.a: Sudden vibrations propagating through the earth caused by tectonic plate adjustments, originating at an underground focus and spreading outward from the surface epicentre.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Earthquakes and Seismic Energy Transmission'.
questions.a: Tectonic vibrations radiate outward from the surface epicentre located directly above the subterranean origin focus.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Earthquakes and Seismic Energy Transmission' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Earthquakes (source: gess203.txt lines 51-85)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Earthquake Measurement and Disaster Preparedness' refers to.
questions.a: Quantification of seismic magnitude using a seismograph on the Richter scale, alongside practical safety measures to mitigate disaster impacts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Earthquake Measurement and Disaster Preparedness'.
questions.a: Richter scale rating measures earthquake magnitude while structural shelter precautions minimise human impact.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Earthquake Measurement and Disaster Preparedness' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Earthquake Preparedness (source: gess203.txt lines 86-140)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Weathering and Erosion Processes' refers to.
questions.a: Degradation of surface geology split into static rock disintegration (weathering) and dynamic removal and transport of material by water, wind, or ice (erosion).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Weathering and Erosion Processes'.
questions.a: Weathering breaks down surface rocks while natural agents erode, transport, and deposit rock particles to shape landforms.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Weathering and Erosion Processes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Major Landforms (source: gess203.txt lines 141-155)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fluvial Landforms and River Processes' refers to.
questions.a: Geological structures created across river courses, including erosion features like waterfalls and meanders, and deposition features like ox-bow lakes, floodplains, levees, and deltas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fluvial Landforms and River Processes'.
questions.a: Running water shapes landscapes through upper-course erosion and lower-course deposition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fluvial Landforms and River Processes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Work of a River (source: gess203.txt lines 156-200)

concepts.title: Coastal Landforms and Sea Wave Action

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Coastal Landforms and Sea Wave Action' refers to.
questions.a: Shoreline structures produced by marine hydraulic action and abrasion, progressing from sea caves to arches and isolated stacks, along with sea cliffs and beaches.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Coastal Landforms and Sea Wave Action'.
questions.a: Continuous wave action erodes coastal rock from caves to arches and stacks, while sediment deposition creates beaches.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Coastal Landforms and Sea Wave Action' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Work of Sea Waves (source: gess203.txt lines 201-225)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Glacial Landforms and Ice Erosion' refers to.
questions.a: Features crafted by moving ice sheets that scrape bedrock hollows which fill into glacial lakes, while dumping mixed rock sediment as glacial moraines.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Glacial Landforms and Ice Erosion'.
questions.a: Moving glaciers carve deep bedrock hollows and deposit unsorted rock debris known as moraines.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Glacial Landforms and Ice Erosion' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Work of Ice (source: gess203.txt lines 226-245)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Aeolian Landforms and Wind Action' refers to.
questions.a: Arid features shaped by wind erosion and transport, producing narrow-based mushroom rocks, shifting sand dunes, and extensive fine silt loess deposits.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Aeolian Landforms and Wind Action'.
questions.a: Desert winds selectively erode rock bases and deposit sand as dunes or fine dust as extensive loess fields.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Aeolian Landforms and Wind Action' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Work of Wind (source: gess203.txt lines 246-270)
